title: Long-context reasoning fidelity
bottleneck: Extending context windows to millions of tokens has outpaced the ability to actually reason over them. Models exhibit lost-in-the-middle behavior, failing to use information buried in long contexts, while the KV cache for a 128K-token Llama-3-70B run consumes about 39 GB — nearly half an H100. Reasoning quality degrades as context grows even when the facts are present in the window.
why_it_blocks: The promised use cases — whole-codebase analysis, full legal discovery, book-length reasoning — require reliable attention across the entire window, not a bigger buffer the model ignores.
current_state: Needle-in-haystack retrieval tests look good, but multi-hop reasoning across long contexts still degrades sharply. Attention optimization shifts the bottleneck without removing it. Even frontier models with 1M-token windows fail multi-hop reasoning tests that span the full context.
